statements.context: Cornyn was reacting to Bill Gates saying on NBC's Meet the Press, when asked whether AI could wipe out humanity, that AI could kill a billion people.
statements.reason: He calls a warning that AI could cause mass deaths irresponsible, which dismisses the catastrophic risk itself rather than only opposing regulation.

statements.context: Same exchange: Cornyn on Bill Gates's warning that AI could kill a billion people, which he suggested could serve large AI companies seeking regulation that crowds out competitors.
statements.reason: He labels a warning of mass deaths from AI as fearmongering, which dismisses catastrophic risk from AI.

statements.context: Same exchange: Cornyn on how the Trump administration is handling AI regulation.

slowdown.note: No statement found for or against slowing frontier AI for safety reasons; he praised the administration for not putting 'a heavy hand' on AI, which is about regulation generally, not a stated position on a slowdown.

notes: Seven web searches ran; none was refused. The Fox News page was opened twice, but the page-reading tool returned Cornyn's longer sentences split into fragments, so only the short quotes it showed as continuous, directly attributed passages are used; a reviewer should check the three quotes against the article, including the trailing commas. Left out because I could not confirm it as one continuous passage: his remark that he worries Gates's warning is 'in pursuit of what's sometimes called regulatory capture', with a handful of AI companies crowding out competitors. The F reading could be argued: his stated objection is partly that such warnings invite regulation favouring big firms, but he does call the warning itself irresponsible fearmongering. An Ask a Pol interview (askapol.com/p/sen-cornyn-on-schumers-ai-forums) appeared in search results with remarks that 'I don't think the scare tactics have been particularly useful' and that AI is either 'the greatest thing since sliced bread, or it's going to take over the world and destroy us'; the page returned a 404 error, and it concerns Schumer's AI forums, so it most likely predates 1 January 2025; excluded. No source found showing he co-sponsored the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (S. 5493, Sanders); search results name only Sanders and Casar as sponsors, and congress.gov was not checked. Two Sinclair station articles from September 2026 on Congress and AI risk were opened and do not mention Cornyn. Reports conflict on his view of the 2025 federal moratorium on state AI laws (not relevant to the positions tracked here).
